NM2-1.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used as a nonparametric nonlinear regression technique with additive Gaussian noise to model brain development as a function of age and sex. The model was trained on n=129 (functional) and n=127 (anatomical) participants under 10-fold cross-validation.
NM2-1.supporting_text: A model of brain development as a function of age and sex was created by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model, which is a nonparametric nonlinear regression technique with additive Gaussian noise, on a sample of n = 129 and n = 127 (77 cases, Table 1, online Supplementary Fig. S3 for an age distribution) to predict brain function and structure, respectively
NM2-1.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Constructing normative models of brain structure and function

NM2-2.detail: For fMRI, task-based GLM contrasts from an emotional face-matching task were used as response variables, including three conditions: negative faces, positive/neutral faces, and shapes. For anatomical MRI, Jacobian determinants (JDs) of the deformation fields were used, which quantify the degree of tissue expansion or contraction required to match each image to the population template.
NM2-2.supporting_text: Three vectors comprising onsets and durations of either shapes or negative or positive/neutral faces were convolved with the SPM8 canonical hemodynamic response function in the context of a General Linear Model in order to model the BOLD time course; We decided to take the nonlinear Jacobian determinants as feature for the normative model given that they quantify the overall degree of tissue expansion or contraction required to match each image to the population template.

NM2-3.detail: The normative model was constructed using age and sex as explanatory variables. Site effects were handled separately via ComBat harmonization before normative modeling.
